subject: Defining acceptance metrics, contractual gates, and handoff playbook for QuantaHealth eval
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@quantahealth.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-13T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Evaluation scope & initial MAP — QuantaHealth

Michael — thanks for the demo yesterday. The Quanta team is aligned to run a 4-week evaluation but we need a concise MAP and acceptance definition that we can attach to the SOW. High-level asks from our side:

- Clear pass/fail criteria (quantitative where possible) for latency, throughput and relevance/concordance to our clinical ontology.
- A short list of acceptance tests we can run against sample traffic and synthetic edge cases.
- Exit gates (when we stop the pilot) and a rollback/mitigation plan if thresholds aren’t met.

Attaching a short PDF with scope items from our side — can you push back with a proposed acceptance matrix and a suggested timeline? Ideally we need the contractual SLA language by next Wednesday (11/19).

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Technical Evaluation
QuantaHealth
[Attachment: initial-eval-scope.pdf (PDF)]

From: michael_grant@redwood.com
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@quantahealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-13T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation scope & initial MAP — QuantaHealth

Alex — appreciated the recap and clear asks. Draft responses below; I attached a working acceptance matrix and a MAP draft for your review. High-level summary:

1) Quantitative acceptance thresholds (proposed)
  - Inference latency: 95th percentile < 300ms for 1–2k RPS sampled traffic; 99th < 600ms for peak bursts (synthetic).
  - Accuracy / concordance: semantic match F1 >= 0.86 on our labeled test-suite; mean embedding cosine separation >= 0.72 for intent clusters.
  - Stability: <1% error rate (exceptions/timeouts) over 72-hour rolling window.
  - Cost guardrail: average token cost delta vs baseline <= +15% (so we can evaluate perf/cost tradeoffs).

2) Acceptance tests (runnable):
  - Smoke: 50 concurrent requests over synthetic sample — validate latency SLOs and correct routing to model variant.
  - Regression: 500 labeled prompts — automated scoring script (included) with pass threshold 86% F1.
  - Edge-case fuzz: 200 adversarial prompts for hallucination checks; manual review threshold of <= 5% high-risk hallucinations.
  - Security: data retention test and audit log check (see security checklist).

3) Exit gates / handoff triggers
  - Go: All above thresholds met for two consecutive 48-hour windows + signoff from Quanta PO.
  - Pause/Escalate: Any single threshold breach with impact >10% triggers immediate incident review and can pause the evaluation.
  - Stop: Persistent failures (>48 hours without remediation) or critical security concerns.

4) Timeline proposal (MAP summary)
  - Week 0 (prep): onboarding, test dataset exchange, baseline metric collection.
  - Week 1–2: smoke/regression runs + iterative tuning (daily sync).
  - Week 3: full stress + edge-case validation + security evidence review.
  - Week 4: final verification window & signoff; legal to receive SLA language by 11/19 as requested.

Next steps: I’ll flag a short doc in Drive and create a HubSpot task linking the MAP to the deal. If this looks sane I’ll send an updated doc with contractual SLA bullets for legal to redline.

Attachments: proposed-acceptance-matrix.xlsx, MAP-draft.md

—Michael
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (Excel)]
[Attachment: MAP-draft.md (Markdown)]

Subject: Security & procurement notes for QuantaHealth MAP

Looping in procurement/security notes to ensure we capture contract evidence needs before Week 3: 

- Need SOC 2 Type II attestations and an exportable audit log sample (30 days) — Alex, can you confirm the expected retention window for your audit team?
- Data residency: Quanta requires US-only processing for PHI-adjacent data — include VPC/private deployment checkbox in the MAP.
- Evidence artifacts: checklist attached (lists encryption config, KMS integration, and sample retention policy).

Procurement ask: Lauren — please prepare the minimal SLA bullets (uptime SLO, incident MTTR targets, credits model) that legal can fold into an addendum. We should offer a 30-day evaluation with the standard pilot terms, plus a conditional 3-month Dedicated pilot if acceptance criteria are met.

Thanks — Neha
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: security-evidence-checklist.pdf (PDF)]

Michael / team — this reads well. A couple of items: 

- Can you add a short contractual SLA clause we can surface to procurement? We want explicit MTTR and credits if stability thresholds fail during the evaluation window.
- Please include a rollback plan for the production-like burst test (Week 3 stress). If the model variant increases error rate during the stress test > 10% we need a fast fallback to the baseline model and a runbook for tracing tokens.

Procurement will expect a DocuSign-ready addendum; I see you’ve linked a Drive doc — can you also publish a single-page SLA summary? Once we have that we’ll circulate to our legal and schedule signoff.

Thanks — Alex
